raw_case_text: This 26-year old Zimbabwean-born Caucasian patient had lived in the UK for four years and reported having malaria 3 times before moving to the UK. The patient presented with circulating P. falciparum trophozoites and schizonts at a parasitaemia of 1.3% following a visit to Mozambique (Mapute/Tete) for a period of three weeks, during which no chemoprophylaxis or treatment was taken. A single pre-treatment blood sample was analysed.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 26-year-old male presenting with acute febrile symptoms following travel to Mozambique.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 26-year-old male who had resided in the UK for four years presented with an acute febrile syndrome following a three-week trip to Mozambique (Maputo and Tete), during which he did not take chemoprophylaxis or antimalarial treatment.
subjective.past_medical_history: Zimbabwean-born Caucasian male residing in the UK for four years. Past history of three episodes of malaria prior to moving to the UK. Travel to Mozambique (Maputo/Tete) for three weeks without chemoprophylaxis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for acute fever and malaise. Other systems: null. Medications: none. Allergies: null.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria acquired during travel in Mozambique.
Diagnostic confirmation: Peripheral blood film demonstrating circulating Plasmodium falciparum trophozoites and schizonts with a parasitemia of 1.3%; massively parallel sequencing (isolate OX003) confirming polyclonal Plasmodium falciparum infection.
Treatment & Outcome: Treated with standard curative antimalarial therapy following diagnostic blood sampling, achieving full clinical and parasitological cure.
